title: The main framework — what to keep, what to remove, and how much to shorten

common.preserved_uncertainty: Final heights vary widely between sources, so no fixed height is given (C1). The bush-rose pages checked give about 3 to 7 canes to keep (AF-15, as corrected). One source (Illinois) shortens by half to two-thirds (shown). Yearly one-third renewal and replacing a sickly bush rest on one page each and are not shown (AF-20, AF-39).

decision_notes.text: Keep the strong, healthy canes spread around the base, aiming for an open centre. One rose society says not to worry about cutting out the centre.
Shorten kept canes by about a third to a half; one source says half to two-thirds. Hybrid Teas are cut lower, or to fewer canes, than Floribundas. Grandifloras are pruned much like Hybrid Teas.

doesnt_match_choices.label: Remove this old cane at its base

doesnt_match_notes.text: Remove old, woody or unproductive canes at their base, in favour of younger ones.

not_sure_choices.label: Keep it for now and reassess next pruning
